subject.title: [Bug]: GitHub Copilot anthropic-messages transport silently hangs ~365s in isolated cron sessions (2026.5.27)

question: Should OpenClaw treat aborted no-output embedded agent results from Copilot `anthropic-messages` isolated cron runs as fallback-worthy, and under what replay-safety guard?
rationale: The source path can be changed narrowly, but retrying after `meta.aborted` may replay side effects unless maintainers define the safe boundary and proof requirements.

options.title: Replay-safe fallback only
options.body: Classify aborted no-output results as fallback-worthy only when metadata proves no tool, delivery, or other durable side effects occurred, then require live Copilot cron proof.

options.title: Transport timeout only
options.body: Add a Copilot Anthropic first-token timeout or heartbeat path and keep aborted-result fallback disabled unless a separate policy is approved.

options.title: Status-only behavior
options.body: Keep the current cron `status: error` behavior without automatic fallback, accepting that operators may need to switch primaries manually.

recommendation.title: Replay-safe fallback only
recommendation.body: Classify aborted no-output results as fallback-worthy only when metadata proves no tool, delivery, or other durable side effects occurred, then require live Copilot cron proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history across both the GitHub Copilot provider path and embedded result fallback classifier involved in the policy choice.
